conversation.content:
The Eagles, an American rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1971, are one of the world's best-selling bands, with over 200 million records sold, including 100 million in the US. They have five number-one singles, six number-one albums, six Grammy Awards, and five American Music Awards. Founding members Glenn Frey, Don Henley, Bernie Leadon, and Randy Meisner initially played with Linda Ronstadt before signing with Asylum Records. Their debut album, "Eagles" (1972), produced hits like "Take It Easy". Later albums such as "Desperado" and "On the Border" continued their success, with "One of These Nights" (1975) becoming their first number-one US album.

"Hotel California" (1976) is their most successful album, selling 32 million copies worldwide. Meisner was replaced by Timothy B. Schmit in 1977. After breaking up in 1980, they reunited in 1994 with "Hell Freezes Over" and continued touring and releasing music. Following Glenn Frey's death in 2016, the band re-formed with Frey's son and Vince Gill. The Eagles are on a final tour as of 2023.
